scope: The complete black Sculpted faucet: the base, its mounting face printed on a scaffold with a sloped roof and a sloped skin of two courses, and the display cover snapped onto the tip. Derek's first message is about the base's underside and its support, with the first eight photographs. His second approves the cover's fit on the tip and the base, and names one flaw: a hole in the tip that the cover does not quite cover; the twelve photographs after the first eight go with it. His third is about the tip's thin front. He has not reported the plate or the lever.
tried: the base in hand, its underside after the support came off; the cover snapped onto the tip
observations: So this is the best looking faucet base bottom that we've had ever, at least at this angle. I mean, of course, hope you can see in the photos, it looks pretty amazing towards the back side, towards the aft side. And it's still looking better than we've ever had before towards the fore side, towards the front side. But it is definitely looser there. And I think this has to do with how we continue the print after that initial first layer of the print. It seems like we give up on our non-planar stuff pretty quickly there. And I'm wondering what we can do about that. I'm not sure that we've really put the effort in to really integrate this into the larger faucet print as well. Like, it seems like we, I don't know. I didn't look at all the details of the print, but I'm not sure the sequencing is really thought through completely as part of the whole there. And I'd just like to see if we can do more to continue the non-planar there in a way that's going to help us. You can also see in the photo, the last one there, that the support broke super cleanly off the bottom there. It just fell right off. I have to say, though, it's all one solid support, and that would be impossible to remove if it hadn't broke so cleanly. So that's pretty much why we don't do these solid supports, but because of how easily this dropped off, I'm okay with it here. I just wanted to be clear about that exception. But yeah, I hope you can see what I mean about it feels like the agent pretty much literally applied the non-planar thing to exactly where I asked for, which is good, but then didn't really even consider the transition very much or what was possible after that. I mean, I don't know. Maybe I'm misreading things, and there could be a lot of compromise and stuff I'm not thinking of. So I'd really like you to tell me what you think we should do next here, but I hope we can do some more layers like that first print layer, so that the first print layer turns out even better because it gets built on top of the way that we like. And the other thing I was going to say about the support, I think because it did break so cleanly, I'd like to try to continue it into the heat sets there. There's two levels of counterbore there, though, so we just want to go into the first one, not both of them. If you see what I mean there, I hope. And I think there's a chance those will be removable, so I'd like to try that on the next one here. And so please prepare a new test print of the faucet plate for me here with the changes I'm asking for. Thanks.

Regarding the faucet tip and faucet display cover, that is the best fit that we've had of anything ever. It's amazing. I love it. I think the only tiny imperfection is a hole you can see, which isn't even a gap between the display cover and the faucet tip, even though it might look like a gap between them. It's not. It's actually like a hole in the faucet tip that just didn't get quite covered by the display cover. And other than that, I mean, I think it looks pretty damn good. And so, yeah, please make sure this gets committed and applied to and implemented on everything it needs to be implemented on. And the same for the faucet base. What we just had there needs to be implemented as well, because it's better than anything we've had before, regardless of what we try next. And yeah, so make sure the tip and display changes get applied to the industrial as well. And then make sure you get tag that as like a whatever faucet version approved fit number this would be, and make sure it's all got approved fit there for what I showed you in the photos.

And then regarding what we try next with the faucet tip, I'd like to reconsider this fascia that we've got there, the part that's, in a lot of ways purely cosmetic. I realize it being there does do quite a lot for how our display cover is supported right now, and allowed to bend around something. I mean, it's, maybe even necessary. I don't understand the geometry and forces and physics there, but hopefully you do better than I. And I'm just wondering, it looks so thin on the display cover there. I mean, should more of that or some of that or all of that thin piece of the front of the faucet tip not be there and be part of the display cover instead? I don't know what's possible and what would still snap good. It's very important that it snaps at least as good as it did now, because this worked great. It snapped great, and I'd like to keep that. So I don't know what's possible or what's necessary, but maybe you see what I mean about the thinness we have up front, and you can at least empathize with me a bit and talk to me about our options or show me what you think might be a good option.

agent_reading.author: Claude, from the photos and the print's own record; not Derek's words.
agent_reading.aft_and_fore: Aft is the face's low end as printed, where each line of the skin starts near the bed. Fore is its high end, on top of the scaffold, where each line ends.
agent_reading.fore_gaps: The dark gaps along the fore side's ring are where the stage held each line's upper end a fifth of a millimetre short of the ring.
agent_reading.fore_recess: Between the fore recess and the rim, and between it and the bore, the face is a strip narrower than a few lines are long, so the stage laid it as short separate dabs.
agent_reading.backing: One more sloped course lay on the first before the level courses took over, and those reached the fore side last. The first course is a bridge over air and was pressed by little before then.
agent_reading.edge: The slanted marks along the foot's edge are the blunt ends of the level courses' walls where each stops on the skin.
agent_reading.recesses: The insert recesses were bridged with no support in them, as the plate's standing recipe has them.
agent_reading.limits: Photographs only. Which recess each close view of the base shows is not stated, nor which side of the head each close view of the cover shows. Nothing was measured.
agent_reading.cover: Derek's second message calls the cover's fit on the tip the best fit so far. It does not name the plate the tip and cover came from; they are read as this plate's from the message's place among his reports on this print. The photographs show the cover seated along the neck with its lower edge close against the tip on both sides and its front flush with the tip's front plane.
agent_reading.hole: The hole Derek names shows in 10, 13 and 14: a small dark opening in the tip's surface just outside the cover's lower edge, at the inside corner where that edge turns toward the front plane. The cover's edge passes beside it without covering it.
agent_reading.front_seam: 19 is a close, out-of-focus view along the front plane; the dark marks along its seam are not named by Derek.

image_processing: Saved as this session received them, JPEGs about two thousand pixels on their long side.

The whole underside square on: the ring-shaped face, the bore with its slot, and the three insert recesses with strands across their mouths.
One insert recess close up: loose strands across its mouth and shoulder, and the face's lines beside it standing apart.
The face by the rim and an insert recess: lines standing apart and wavy, and dark gaps between the rim's ring and the ends of the lines.
The foot from the side and below: the bottom edge as a thin even band.
The face seen along its lines: tight, even lines, with lifted strands at the bore's edge.
The foot's bottom edge from the side after the support came off, the picture Derek names for the clean break.
The head's front plane close up: the cover's front wall in fine lines beside the tip's outlet face, its courses curving around the dispense opening.
The cover's lower edge on the neck where it turns toward the front, with a small dark hole in the tip just outside the corner.
The cover from the side and front: its window, its front corner, and its lower edge running along the neck.
The cover's front corner and lower edge on the neck, close.
The same corner as 10 from another angle: the hole in the tip beside the cover's edge, with a bright fleck in it.
The same corner again, the hole in the tip a small dark mark just outside the cover's edge.

The cover seated on the neck from above and behind, its lower edge close along the tip.
